title: Answer to Question: Why the Intense Keenness of the Interim Government in Kyrgyzstan to Hold a Referendum on the New Constitution?
text:
Answer to Question: Why the Intense Keenness of the Interim Government in Kyrgyzstan to Hold a Referendum on the New Constitution?

Question:

A referendum was held on 27/6/2010 on the new constitution in Kyrgyzstan, and before the blood that flowed in the tragic events had dried! The interim government did not accept postponing the referendum until conditions returned to their normal state and the displaced returned from their lands to their destroyed homes; rather, the government insisted on holding the referendum despite all these circumstances!

So why this intense keenness of the government to hold the referendum, instead of keenness to rebuild what was destroyed and burnt, and to deal with the blood that flowed in the ethnic events between the Uzbeks and the Kyrgyz in the south?

Answer:

Before entering into the details, we point to a striking reality that has recently appeared in the conduct of the Russian Federation, namely the return to the method of the Soviet Union of crushing with iron and fire against its opponents in the states that were within the Soviet Union, even after its disintegration and collapse! This has appeared in several events, from the occupation of the north of Georgia to the events of Kyrgyzia. As for the events of Georgia, the occupation of its north is plain to see. As for the events of Kyrgyzia, before mentioning the latest events we go back a little to the events of the coup against Bakiyev, in order to clarify the picture:

1- Russia supported the election of Bakiyev on 23/7/2009, and the Russians' support for his election was striking, as the Russian president Medvedev came in person to Kyrgyzia and took part in the inauguration ceremonies held for Bakiyev on 2/8/2009!

2- Russia noticed in Bakiyev a drawing closer to America, which appeared in two influential events:

The first: The visit of Richard Holbrooke, the American president's envoy for Afghanistan, to Kyrgyzia on 19/2/2010, where he met with each of the two presidents of the two countries. The page "Russia Today" reported, citing the Russian "Interfax" on 19/2/2010, that Holbrooke discussed with President Kurmanbek Bakiyev "the prospects of bilateral relations and the situation in Afghanistan, and the two sides exchanged views, away from the spotlight, about the situation in Afghanistan and dealt with ways of activating mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries." And it reported that the press office of the Kyrgyz presidency quoted Bakiyev as declaring that "his country gives importance and priority to developing Kyrgyz-American relations and activating bilateral cooperation." And you see the Russian agency Interfax, while reporting the news, adding the phrase "and the two sides exchanged, away from the spotlight", that is, secretly, away from the eyes of the Russians, so that they would not know what their agent Bakiyev agreed upon with the Americans. This is a hint and an insinuation from the Russians that something happened between the Kyrgyz president and the Americans.

The second: The page "Russia Today" reported on 17/3/2010 that "the United States recently announced the allocation of 5.5 million dollars to help Kyrgyzia build a centre for training special counter-terrorism units in the city of Batken." "Russia Today" asked Alexander Knyazev, director of the Bishkek branch of the Institute of CIS Countries, about the subject of this centre, and he said: "Washington may use this centre to meet its needs in Central Asia. The slogan of counter-terrorism is nothing but a pretext for achieving American goals, as it is in Iraq and Afghanistan." And he added: "Washington seeks, through these projects in Central Asia, to confront the competition of Russia and China in the region."

3- The Russians felt apprehensive about Holbrooke's visit to Kyrgyzia and his meeting with its president Bakiyev, away from the spotlight, and the conclusion of secret agreements between the two sides, which were crowned with the establishment of an American centre in Kyrgyzia for training special forces and recruiting agents under the pretext of the so-called fight against terrorism, so that America would strengthen its influence in Kyrgyzia and then set out from it to other regions.

The agreement to establish an American centre for training special forces, or in other words for graduating agents for America in Kyrgyzia, this matter was the sounding of the alarm bell and a setting out towards crossing the red lines for Russia. Therefore it hastened with the coup, in order to prevent Bakiyev from going further in his relationship with America, and the euphoria of "victory" in carrying out the coup against Bakiyev and toppling him on 8/4/2010 was evident on Russia.

Thus Russia disciplined its former agent Bakiyev for the distancing from it that it had noticed in him!

4- It remained for Russia to deal with the matter of Karimov in Uzbekistan, his cutting of his ropes with Russia and his going along with America, after he had been going along with it, especially as it had helped him militarily in the events of Andijan. However, America's economic and security enticements to him made him show an increasing inclination towards America and a noticeable distancing from Russia.

That has appeared since the beginning of last year, when Russia decided on 4/2/2009 to establish the rapid reaction forces, or by another name the rapid deployment forces. They signed this agreement in Moscow on 14/6/2009, and Uzbekistan refrained from signing it. And Uzbekistan did not take part in the manoeuvres of 26 August 2009 in the area of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation, which continued until 15 October 2009. The conduct of Uzbekistan is considered a semi-freezing of its membership in this organisation, but it did not announce that officially. Not only this, but Uzbekistan objected to the establishment of a second base for Russia in Kyrgyzia, because it threatens its entity, as this base would be set up close to the Uzbek border in the area of the Fergana Valley. The Novosti agency reported on 5/8/2009 that Uzbekistan announced, as came in a statement published on 3/8/2009 by the "Jahon" agency affiliated with the Uzbek foreign ministry, "that it sees no necessity or usefulness in implementing the plan for deploying another Russian military base in addition to the Russian base in Kant in the south of Kyrgyzia, pointing out that deploying a new base may lead to destabilising the region."

On 18/8/2009, the head of the regime in Uzbekistan, Karimov, declared during his meeting with the American general David Petraeus in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan: "Uzbekistan is ready to expand constructive cooperation with the United States on the basis of the principles of mutual respect and equal partnership." (The Russian Novosti agency 18/8/2009).

America signed an agreement with Uzbekistan for transporting the cargoes of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) from Uzbekistan to Afghanistan. [Source: the National Center for Strategic Studies, dated 04/04/2009]. However, the relations between the Uzbek and American administrations were not limited to that; rather, the American administration issued a message of congratulation to Uzbekistan on the occasion of the 18th anniversary of its independence, and then Karimov accepted the visit of the American ambassador in Uzbekistan, "Richard Norland", and before that, on 18 August, Karimov accepted the visit of the commander of the Central Command of the United States of America, General "David Howell Petraeus", and a cooperation agreement was signed between the two countries containing military and training programmes and vocational education.

Thus Karimov is moving away from Russia and drawing closer to America.

5- In Russia's manner, it was necessary to put an end to Karimov's drawing closer to America, and so it was. Russia wanted to create a problem for Uzbekistan by displacing large numbers of the Uzbek minority from Kyrgyzia to Uzbekistan, so as to create a justification for intervening to solve the problem by way of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation, whose membership Uzbekistan had frozen some time ago... And because the problem would be glaring, Uzbekistan would be compelled by it to return to the Collective Security Treaty Organisation to solve the problem, which naturally is under the leadership of Russia, so that Uzbekistan returns to the Russian house of obedience and consequently moves away from America.

6- Therefore Russia pushed the interim government and Russia's henchmen in Kyrgyzia, and not the honourable Kyrgyz, to attack the Uzbeks with burning, destruction and killing... in order to drive them towards the Uzbek border. The plan almost succeeded, so that Uzbekistan would agree to take part in the Collective Security Treaty Organisation and send forces under the leadership of Russia to solve the problem, had it not been for the intervention of the American ambassador in Tashkent on behalf of the American government, which contacted the Uzbek government and convinced it not to participate with the forces of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation. This government responded and closed the border in the face of the Uzbek displaced after it had opened it at the beginning, and about 100 thousand displaced people had reached it. It appears that they, that is the Russians and the agent government in Kyrgyzia, wanted hundreds of thousands of Uzbeks to flee to Uzbekistan in order to create a crisis between the two countries; then the Collective Security Treaty Organisation, after Uzbekistan's return to it, under the leadership of Russia, would intervene to solve the problem; then negotiations would take place for returning them, and in this way Russia would exploit the situation by pressuring Uzbekistan to return it to its fold and impose other conditions on it in return for returning the displaced to their homes in Kyrgyzia. But Uzbekistan, as we said, refused, through the intervention of the American government, and therefore the American Assistant Secretary of State Robert Blake praised the conduct of Uzbekistan and its closing of the border in the face of the displaced.

7- What confirms that Russia wanted to exploit those displaced to Uzbekistan in order to return Uzbekistan to the Collective Security Treaty Organisation is that the interim Kyrgyz prime minister, Roza Otunbayeva, as the Russian Novosti agency reported on 12/6/2010, requested the Russian president Medvedev to send forces to help her calm the situation. But Russia, as came on the tongue of Natalia Timakova, the spokeswoman of the Russian president, "refused that on the claim that the conflict is internal and that the circumstances do not require effective Russian participation", that is, they do not require the participation of Russia alone. What confirms that is what the Russian newspaper Vedomosti reported, quoting an official in the Russian defence ministry as saying: "Deploying forces in Kyrgyzia and financing them is a difficult matter without the help of Uzbekistan." This indicates that Uzbekistan is the target in these events, to force it to resume its activity and activate its membership in the Collective Security Treaty Organisation, and then participate in the rapid reaction force under the command of Russia. But when Uzbekistan did not respond, Russia decided, in the name of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation, on 14/6/2010, to send military and air equipment to Kyrgyzia.

8- When Russia failed to drag Uzbekistan into the Collective Security Treaty Organisation and the rapid reaction forces, it wanted to exploit what happened by presenting it as ethnic fighting, and that the Uzbek minority is not (patriotic) like the Kyrgyz... And it insisted on holding the referendum on time without postponing it, in order to create popularity for the interim government, on the basis that the interim government is with the interests of the Kyrgyz and that it is against the (unpatriotic) Uzbeks. Therefore Azimbek Beknazarov, deputy head of the Kyrgyz interim government, declared: "The situation in Osh has begun to stabilise, we have enough forces, and we must organise the referendum; all those who call themselves Kyrgyz citizens must vote in the referendum." (Al Jazeera 17/6/2010). In this way it created something of an ethnic rallying of the Kyrgyz around the interim government, and that was in the results of the referendum on the constitution, which was on 27/6/2010.

9- In summary, the events of Kyrgyzia are contrived events, planned by Russia together with the interim government, by attacking the Uzbek minority in order to displace it to Uzbekistan, so as to create a problem for Uzbekistan with which it would be compelled to return to the Collective Security Treaty Organisation and the rapid reaction force to put an end to the problem. It was not ethnic fighting, because what happened is that Russia's henchmen and the interim government from among the Kyrgyz attacked the Uzbeks with horrific brutal acts, and it was not fighting between two sides such that it could be called an ethnic war.

Some agencies declared, in commenting on what they witnessed, that the acts were planned and not spontaneous. The agency France-Presse reported on 17/6/2010 that "the testimonies of its correspondents and the losses they observed in recent days in the south of Kyrgyzia indicate that the Uzbeks fell victim to coordinated liquidation operations which resulted in hundreds of deaths." And it added: "Matching testimonies in Osh, where the events broke out a week ago, and in Jalal-Abad and in the refugee camps in Uzbekistan, indicate that tanks opened the way for armed militias which swept the Uzbek neighbourhoods in coordinated attacks, while the neighbourhoods inhabited by a majority of ethnic Kyrgyz remained almost intact. Houses in the neighbourhoods of the Uzbek minority were destroyed down to their foundations after being looted, in well-organised operations. Tanks fired incendiary shells which set the houses on fire, while gunmen with Kalashnikov rifles fired bullets at their inhabitants who were trying to put out the fires."

Some of our young men went to the state centres in the area to intervene to prevent the burning and destruction, but those centres did not respond to our young men; rather, they arrested some of them!

The New York Times reported on 16/6/2010 the statement of Rupert Colville, the spokesman of the office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, saying: "The attacks, which resulted in the deaths of at least a hundred people and the displacement of a hundred thousand Uzbeks or more from their homes, were coordinated, targeted and well planned, and were not a spontaneous outbreak of ethnic violence."

When Russia failed to return Uzbekistan to its fold, it exploited the events to create a rallying of the Kyrgyz around the interim government in the referendum on the constitution, presenting what happened as an ethnic conflict between the unpatriotic Uzbek minority and the patriotic Kyrgyz, whose interests the interim government adopts.

10- However, the sad thing in the matter is that this struggle for influence in Central Asia between Russia and America is carried out with local tools, and its victims are Muslims. All that is because the bond that unites the Muslims, which is Islam, the Kafir colonialists and their agents try to remove from the forefront and to make tribalist (asabiyyah) bonds take its place, so that the blood of the Muslims flows at the hands of Muslims.

At the conclusion of this answer, we call upon the Uzbek and Kyrgyz brothers, whom Islam has united for centuries, to realise that the honour of this world and the Hereafter is in Islam which unites them, and that what Russia and America and their agents are doing is in order to make the Muslims' violence among themselves severe, shedding their blood with their own hands for the benefit of the Kafirs.

We ask Allah (swt) for His victory and His relief, by the establishment of the Khilafah, so that it unites the Muslims upon good, loving brothers, the best Ummah brought forth for mankind. "And Allah has full power and control over His affair, but most of mankind know not."
